source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 7, line 24; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 30,000.00 + armed forces retirement pay (person 0) 40,000.00 + armed forces retirement pay (person 1) 35,000.00 = 105,000.00. Federal taxable income = 105,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 73,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing jointly. Line 9 federal AGI 105,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 31,500.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 105,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 55,000.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 24 armed forces retirement pay (person 0): smaller of 40,000.00 and 30,000.00 = 30,000.00; line 24 armed forces retirement pay (person 1): smaller of 35,000.00 and 30,000.00 = 30,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 60,000.00. Line 17 = 105,000.00 + 0.00 - 31,500.00 - 0.00 - 60,000.00 = 13,500.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 73,500.00 - 60,000.00 = 13,500.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 13,500.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 8,000.00 = 120 + 3.2% x 5,500.00 = 176; total 296, to the cent 296.00. The table row over 13,400 to 13,500 gives 294; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 296.00. 'If you are married filing jointly and both spouses qualify, each qualifying armed forces retiree may claim' 30,000.
